sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Cohesive Forces**: Intermolecular forces between molecules of the **same substance**.
• **Adhesive Forces**: Intermolecular forces between molecules of **different substances** (e.g., liquid and glass).
• **Mechanism**: If Adhesion > Cohesion, the liquid wets the surface and rises (concave meniscus). If Cohesion > Adhesion, the liquid is depressed (convex meniscus).
• **Jurin's Law**: The height (h) of the liquid column is inversely proportional to the radius (r) of the capillary tube (h ∝ 1/r).

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Liquid rises above the free surface level (e.g., Water in glass)
Liquid level falls below the free surface (e.g., Mercury in glass)
Used in barometers and scientific instrumentation

items.definition: The curved upper surface of a liquid in a tube. Concave for wetting liquids, convex for non-wetting liquids.
The elastic tendency of a fluid surface which makes it acquire the least surface area possible; the primary driver of capillarity.

items.title: Major Applications
items.content:
• **Biological**: Ascent of sap in plants through xylem vessels.
• **Daily Life**: Ink absorption by blotting paper, oil rising in lamp wicks, and cotton clothes absorbing sweat.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Capillary action can cause moisture damage in building foundations (rising damp).
• **Solutions**: Use of damp-proof courses (DPC) and hydrophobic coatings to break capillary paths.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'AC-UP' (Adhesion > Cohesion = UP).
• **Decoded Meaning**: If Adhesion is greater than Cohesion, the liquid moves UP the tube.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often asks if capillary rise depends on gravity. Yes, it does. If gravity is zero (e.g., in space), the liquid will rise to the top of the tube regardless of length.
Mains Value Addition: Link capillarity to 'Water Security' and 'Agricultural Efficiency' (e.g., soil moisture retention and irrigation techniques).

keyTakeaways: Capillarity is a direct consequence of the competition between adhesive and cohesive forces.
The height of rise is inversely proportional to the radius of the tube (Jurin's Law).
Capillary action is essential for plant physiology and various industrial filtration processes.
